rationale: Read the transfer-replay receipt (execution cfeb8d63a1134a859021ca15bc7f098b, exit 0, both cases passed): all four comparisons are complete and hold, so the replay effect is decided - the first TimeoutNow payload moved leadership to the target (term 2 -> 3) and the identical payload honoured again raised the term to 4 while the same node remained Leader, whereas the control's plain campaign with an equal log claim was not granted, left the term at 2 and changed no leadership. Because that receipt says nothing about the cost of the extra election, the harness now samples the leadership set every 10 ms for 1.5 s after the duplicate and issues one client write at the same time, so the impact is measured rather than inferred. Local construction runs of that extension show one leaderless sample out of 141 and a client write that still succeeded, which is why this update records the finding as a bounded robustness defect rather than an availability break, and requests the receipt for the impact fields.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: the leadership-transfer control message is not idempotent and carries no context with which a receiver could reject a duplicate or stale copy, so the same payload honoured twice forces a second election; the measured cost in a healthy three-voter cluster is one extra term and a brief leaderless interval, not a change of leader or a failed client operation. Decided evidence (execution cfeb8d63a1134a859021ca15bc7f098b, all four comparisons complete and holding; setup index 0 and probe index 1 for the duplicate case, setup index 2 and probe index 3 for the control): the duplicate case's first delivery moved leadership to the target (leader_before was the original leader, leader_after_first is the target at term 3), the identical payload was then delivered to that new leader and the term after the duplicate is 4 with the same node still Leader, so an election ran although the cluster needed no transfer; the control delivered a plain RequestVote carrying the follower's own log claim with the transfer flag unset, which was not granted and left the term at 2 with the target still a follower and the original leader unchanged. Source basis: TimeoutNowRequest embeds only RPCHeader with no term and no sender role (src_timeout_now_msg, commands.go 205-208), timeoutNow clears the known leader, moves the node to Candidate and sets the candidate-from-transfer flag without validating anything (src_timeout_now, raft.go 2232-2239), and that flag is what makes voters skip the known-leader rejection in requestVote (src_request_vote, raft.go 1626-1758). Impact in this configuration: term churn plus one extra election; the leader identity did not change because the re-elected node had the most up-to-date log, and safety still holds because the vote's log-completeness test guards the outcome. Local construction runs of the impact extension show a single leaderless sample out of 141 samples taken at 10 ms intervals after the duplicate and a client write issued at the same moment that still succeeded, so the availability cost is bounded to a brief gap rather than a lost write; those fields are requested with this update and are currently construction feedback only. Limits: three voters, in-process transport, no partition or write load during the replay, one duplicate; the partition-heal interaction, larger clusters and the case where the duplicated message reaches a node that cannot win are unmeasured, and no safety consequence was found because a stale copy still cannot win a vote with a stale log.
counterevidence: The first delivery is the documented transfer path; only the identical second delivery is the defect subject, and that delivery is supplied by the harness rather than produced by the library's own transport.

The measured impact is small: the same node was re-elected, one leaderless sample appeared in 141 and a concurrent client write still succeeded, so this is a robustness and churn defect rather than an availability break.
Raft tolerates spurious elections harmlessly for safety, and the vote's log-completeness test still applies to the replay, so no unsafe leadership outcome follows from the duplicate.
limitations: The impact fields (leaderless sampling and the concurrent write) are construction feedback pending the requested receipt.
One cluster size and one delivery path; partitions during replay, delayed rather than duplicated delivery, larger clusters and the interaction with in-flight writes are unmeasured.

scope.description: The same two cases as the previous revision (three-voter cluster, ten committed entries, one TimeoutNow payload delivered twice versus a plain follower campaign as control), extended in the duplicate case so that the aftermath is measured: the leadership set is sampled every 10 ms for 1.5 s after the duplicate and a single client write is issued at the start of that window, with the write outcome and the count of leaderless samples recorded alongside the term and state.
assumptions: Fault model unchanged: no message loss inside the injected transport; the induced event is one duplicated control message, or one plain campaign in the control case.
Sampling at 10 ms can miss transitions faster than that step, so a zero-count would not establish absence of a gap; a non-zero count does establish that the cluster had no leader at that instant.

The client write is issued once, immediately after the duplicate delivery, with the ordinary 200 ms enqueue timeout, so its outcome reflects the state the duplicate created rather than a retry policy.
Reused facilities: MakeCluster with inmemConfig timings and InmemTransport.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
No partition is induced, so the case still isolates message handling rather than concurrency.

experiment.prefix: As before: elect a leader in a three-voter cluster, commit ten entries, record the leader, term and log claims, then in the duplicate case deliver one TimeoutNow built from the current leader's header to a follower, wait for a stable single leader, deliver the identical payload again to that new leader, and now also sample the leadership set every 10 ms for 1.5 s while issuing one client write, recording the leaderless sample count, the write outcome and the term and state at the end; in the control case deliver a plain RequestVote from the follower's own identity and log claim and record the response and whether the leadership changed.
semantic_changes: The duplicate case samples the leadership set after the duplicate delivery and issues one client write, adding leaderless-sample counts and the write outcome to the probe event.
experiment.requirement: A control message that changes leadership must either carry enough context for its receiver to reject a duplicate or stale copy, or must not change leadership when honoured again.

comparisons.description: Sanity: the first delivery performs the requested transfer, so the second delivery is a duplicate rather than the initial transfer.
The identical payload honoured a second time raises the term again, i.e. the duplicate forces another election in a cluster that needed no transfer.
Control: the same log claim carried by a plain campaign is refused because a leader is known, so the difference is the transfer path rather than the request's log content.
Control: no election follows a plain campaign, so the duplicate case's second election is not an artifact of the probe schedule.

experiment.revision_reason: The four comparisons are decided, so this revision measures the cost of the extra election instead of repeating only the decision: the duplicate case now samples the leadership set every 10 ms for 1.5 s and issues one client write during that window, emitting the leaderless sample count, the gap flag and the write outcome. Cases, scenario, anchors, requirement and comparisons are otherwise unchanged.
